data.narrative:
Swift Beat, a Series A defense and security company founded by Eric Schmidt, is evaluated against a peer universe of 11 same-sector and adjacent-stage comparables, comprising 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms including Anduril Industries, Helsing, and Singularity. The company has raised $50M+ to date.

Two triangulation methods are applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $50M total raised as a valuation proxy, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression, yielding $100M. Peer-median analysis across the 11-company comp set produces a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range spanning $125M (floor) to $3.0B (ceiling). The highest-valued peers include Dream Security at $3.0B and Allen Control Systems at $2.2B, both at Series B; lower-stage peers compress valuations toward the $125M–$300M band.

The two methods produce divergent signals. Stage-progression suggests $100M, while peer-median indicates $1.0B. Synthesizing both approaches, the triangulated range is $85M (low), $550M (median), and $1.1B (high). Key uncertainties include revenue scale and growth trajectory relative to peers, customer concentration, and regulatory positioning within defense end-markets. The wide dispersion ($85M–$1.1B) reflects stage mismatch within the peer set; clarity on near-term growth and customer traction would narrow this band materially.
